learning_outcomes.text: That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.
Ability for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Ability to apply new technologies, including information and communication technologies.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism and their application to solving engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK I: MECHANICS
Topic 1.- INTRODUCTION: Physics and its methods. Scalar and vector magnitudes. Vector algebra. Sliding vectors. Derivative of a vector. Vector representation of surfaces. Elementary field theory.
Topic 2.- PARTICLE KINEMATICS: Position vector. Velocity vector. Acceleration vector. Intrinsic components of acceleration. Classification of movements. Composition of movements. Relative motion.
Topic 3.- PARTICLE DYNAMICS: Newton's Laws. Friction forces.
Topic 4.- WORK AND ENERGY: Work done by a force. Power. Work and kinetic energy. Conservative forces. Potential energy. Non-conservative forces. Principle of conservation of mechanical energy.

Topic 5.- DYNAMICS OF PARTICLE SYSTEMS: Internal and external forces. Center of mass. Momentum and angular momentum: conservation theorems. Center of mass reference system. Kinetic energy of a particle system. Collisions.
Topic 6.- RIGID BODY MECHANICS: Concept of rigid body. Kinematics of rigid body. Rotational dynamics of rigid body. Moments of inertia: calculation. Angular momentum. Rotational kinetic energy.
Topic 7.- STATIC EQUILIBRIUM AND ELASTICITY: Equilibrium conditions. Center of gravity. Stress and strain. Elastic moduli.
Topic 8.- FLUIDS: Density. Pressure in a fluid. Archimedes' principle. Dynamics of ideal fluids. Viscosity.
BLOQUE II: WAVE PHENOMENA

Topic 9.- OSCILLATORY MOTION: Elastic recovery forces. Kinematics and dynamics of simple harmonic motion. Energy of a harmonic oscillator. Examples of oscillators. Damped oscillations. Forced oscillations and resonance.
Topic 10.- WAVE MOTION: Concept of wave. Types of waves. Wave equation. Harmonic waves. Intensity and absorption. Interference phenomena. Standing waves.
Practical: Introduction to Measurement Theory seminar.
Practical: Study of the simple pendulum
Practical: Acceleration of a body subjected to constant forces
Practical: Moment of inertia of a body: Torsion pendulum
Practical: Measurement of solid densities with the pycnometer
Practical: Inclined plane
Practical: Study of systems in static equilibrium
Practical: Study of the elastic constant of a spring
Practical: Conservation of mechanical energy.
teaching_methods: Explanation of general theory examples (Exposición de teoría de ejemplos generales)
Large group expository classes with support of various didactic resources.
Small group classes for problem solving, seminars and assignment presentation.
Practical group classes: exercise solving; laboratory experiments; presentations/exhibitions.
Collective/individual tutorials: clarification of doubts and debates.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities
Theoretical concepts of the subject (Theoretical exam)
Laboratory/field practices/use of ICT tools (Lab report)

assessment_rules: To pass the subject, the student must: 1) achieve a minimum score of 4 out of 10 in the theoretical exam and 2) have passed the subject's practical sessions. For the laboratory practice grade, the results of a practice exam and/or the evaluation of the practice report will be taken into account. In the extraordinary call 2, the same evaluation criteria as in the ordinary calls will be used.
